title: In-session provider failover in model-injector proxy
description:
## Problem

When a provider fails mid-session (429/413/500), the model-injector writes a cooldown file but the current Codex session remains bound to the dead provider. The circuit breaker now blocks requests, but the agent session still fails — it cannot transparently switch to a healthy provider.

## Desired Behaviour

The model-injector should maintain its own provider fallback chain. When a request fails:

1. Write cooldown for the failed provider (already done)
2. Select the next available non-cooled-down provider from a priority list
3. Update `current-model` to the new provider
4. Replay the failed request against the new provider transparently

## Implementation Notes

* Requires the model-injector to know the LiteLLM model name mapping (currently only the credit-gate has this)
* Need in-memory health state tracking per provider
* Request replay must handle body decompression/recompression
* Must avoid infinite failover loops (limit to N retries)

## Validation

```bash
python3 -c "import py_compile; py_compile.compile('scripts/ops/model-injector-proxy.py', doraise=True)"
```

title: Circuit breaker with escalating cooldowns
description:
## Problem

Currently each error type has a fixed cooldown duration. If a provider fails 3 times in a row (e.g., Gemini quota, SambaNova rate limits), the cooldown resets to the same fixed value each time. This means providers get retried too frequently when they are persistently failing.

## Desired Behaviour

Implement escalating cooldowns: if provider fails N times within a window, double the cooldown each time:

* 1st failure: base cooldown (e.g., 120s)
* 2nd failure: 2x (240s)
* 3rd failure: 4x (480s)
* Cap at max (e.g., 3600s)

## Implementation Notes

* Requires coordinated state file format change: cooldown files need an "escalation level" field
* Both [model-injector-proxy.py](<http://model-injector-proxy.py>) (writes) and [codex-credit-gate.sh](<http://codex-credit-gate.sh>) (reads) must agree on format
* Consider JSON format for cooldown files instead of plain timestamp

## Validation

```bash
python3 -c "import py_compile; py_compile.compile('scripts/ops/model-injector-proxy.py', doraise=True)"
```

title: Pre-session provider health check in credit-gate
description:
## Problem

The credit-gate selects a provider and spawns Codex, but if ALL providers are rate-limited/broken, the session starts and immediately fails — burning an empty turn and incrementing retry counters. This wastes Symphony resources and accelerates the death spiral.

## Desired Behaviour

Before spawning Codex, verify at least one provider is actually healthy:

1. Check all cooldown files — if ALL providers are cooled down, sleep until the earliest cooldown expires
2. Optionally probe the selected provider with a lightweight request (existing GET /v1/models probe)
3. Only exec Codex when a healthy provider is confirmed

## Implementation Notes

* The credit-gate already has `find_earliest_cooldown()` and rate-limit wait logic
* But currently it waits at the END of the cascade, after already trying all providers
* Move the "all exhausted" wait to the TOP of the loop, before attempting any provider
* Needs integration testing with Symphony's own retry/backoff logic to avoid double-sleeping

## Validation

```bash
bash -n scripts/ops/codex-credit-gate.sh
```

title: Symphony slot-contention should not burn retry attempts
description:
## Problem

With `max_concurrent_agents: 1`, when the single slot is occupied, all other issues get "no available orchestrator slots" error and go into exponential backoff. These slot-contention errors increment the retry counter (attempt=10, 11, 12...) and may cause issues to be abandoned after max retries, even though the issue was never actually attempted.

## Desired Behaviour

"No available orchestrator slots" is structural, not transient — the issue was never attempted. Either:

1. Don't count slot-contention as a retry attempt
2. Use a separate, gentler backoff for slot-contention (e.g., fixed 60s instead of exponential)
3. Increase `max_retry_backoff_ms` to give slot-bound issues more time

## Implementation Notes

* This may require upstream Symphony changes (Elixir orchestrator)
* Alternative: adjust `max_retry_backoff_ms` in [WORKFLOW-3B.md](<http://WORKFLOW-3B.md>) from 600000 to a larger value
* Consider whether `max_concurrent_agents` should be 2 instead of 1 (requires more memory/GPU)

## Validation

Observe Symphony dashboard during a multi-issue run — slot-contention should not rapidly exhaust retry attempts.

title: [SENTINEL] Provider quota tracking in harness report
description:
## Problem

The harness report checks 22 domains but does not monitor provider quota consumption. Providers like Gemini (20 req/day), SambaNova (20 req/day), and Cerebras (1M tok/day) have hard limits that are invisible until exhausted. By the time the model-injector detects the failure, the quota is already gone.

## Desired Behaviour

Add a `provider_health` check domain to the harness report that:

1. Reads all cooldown files and reports their status
2. Queries LiteLLM `/health` for healthy/unhealthy endpoints
3. Counts per-provider errors from model-injector logs (journalctl)
4. Warns when a provider has been cooled down more than N times in 24hr
5. Tracks daily request counts per provider (from proxy logs)

## Implementation Notes

* New check in `scripts/ops/harness-report.mjs`
* Parse journalctl output from `model-injector-proxy.service`
* Read cooldown files from `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/credit-gate/ratelimit-*`
* Query `http://localhost:4010/health` for LiteLLM health status
* Add to the `continuous` profile (check every hour)

## Validation

```bash
node --check scripts/ops/harness-report.mjs && make harness:quick
```

title: [CHILD] GitHub Models (github-gpt41-mini) incompatible with /v1/responses endpoint
description:
## Problem

The `github-gpt41-mini` LiteLLM alias works on `/v1/chat/completions` but returns **404 on** `/v1/responses` (which is the endpoint Codex actually uses).

## Root Cause

LiteLLM config uses `model: openai/gpt-4.1-mini` with `api_base: https://models.github.ai/inference`. For `/v1/responses`, LiteLLM tries to call the OpenAI responses API directly on the custom api_base. GitHub's inference endpoint only supports `/chat/completions`, not `/responses`.

## Current Mitigation

[model-injector-proxy.py](<http://model-injector-proxy.py>) pre-excludes the `github` provider for `/v1/responses` requests, so the cascade skips directly to Ollama. The 404 is avoided entirely.

## Permanent Fix Options

1. Wait for LiteLLM to add GPT-4.1-mini to their `github/` provider registry (then `github/gpt-4.1-mini` would work natively)
2. Configure LiteLLM to force chat-completions translation for this model
3. Add response-API support detection to model-injector

## Evidence

```
curl /v1/chat/completions → OK model=gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14 content=OK
curl /v1/responses → 404 page not found
```

## Acceptance Criteria

* GitHub Models works on both `/v1/chat/completions` AND `/v1/responses`
* OR the limitation is permanently documented and the skip is tested

title: [SENTINEL] Improve Symphony agent error handling and crash resilience
description:
## Problem

Symphony agent sessions crash with `RuntimeError: Agent run failed` on trivial tasks (simple grep, file creation, one-line edits). The agent either fails to initialize or crashes mid-execution after a few tool calls. This wastes retry attempts, burns credits, and blocks the queue.

## Evidence

From production logs (2026-03-07):

* [ANQ-103](https://linear.app/anqr/issue/ANQ-103/identify-and-inventory-all-hardcoded-secrets-in-makefile) (grep Makefile for secrets): 6+ retry attempts, never completed. Agent crashed on every attempt with RuntimeError.
* [ANQ-104](https://linear.app/anqr/issue/ANQ-104/move-hardcoded-makefile-secrets-to-env-and-update-references) (replace hardcoded token): Got to turn 3 (\~37K tokens) then crashed. Multiple `turn completed (failed)` and `agent message streaming: error` entries.
* [ANQ-195](https://linear.app/anqr/issue/ANQ-195/circuit-breaker-with-escalating-cooldowns): Repeated `RuntimeError: Agent run failed` with sub-second log spam. Agent exited immediately on attempt 1, got 3 failed turns on attempt 2 before crashing again.
* [ANQ-174](https://linear.app/anqr/issue/ANQ-174/convert-each-audit-finding-into-one-atomic-linked-issue): `linear_graphql` mutations failed repeatedly — the 3B model couldn't produce correct GraphQL.

## Failure Modes Observed

1. **Immediate crash on startup** — agent exits before producing any output (0 tokens consumed)
2. **Tool call failures** — agent makes tool calls that fail, enters error loop, eventually crashes
3. **Model capability mismatch** — 3B model asked to do complex multi-step GraphQL mutations it can't reliably produce
4. **No graceful degradation** — failures crash the entire session rather than retrying the failing step or escalating to human

## Desired Behaviour

* Agent startup failures should be diagnosed and logged with actionable detail (not just `RuntimeError`)
* Tool call failures should retry the specific tool call, not crash the session
* Tasks beyond model capability should be detected early and escalated to `[HUMAN]` / `Pending`
* Session crashes should preserve partial progress so retries can continue from where they left off

## Child Issues

Each child addresses one specific failure mode with a concrete fix.

Scope:

* In `agent_runner.ex`, capture and log the full error reason from Codex process exit
* Include: exit code, stderr output, last N lines of agent stdout, environment state
* Classify errors into categories: model unreachable, tool init failure, workspace missing, OOM, timeout
* Log a structured JSON line with error category, issue identifier, and diagnostic detail

- [ ] Error categories are distinguishable in log output
- [ ] Existing successful startups are not affected

title: [CHILD] Retry failed tool calls within agent sessions instead of crashing
description:
Finding from ANQ-104/174 log analysis.

Problem: When a tool call fails during an agent session (e.g. apply_patch validation error, GraphQL syntax error), the session enters an error loop and eventually crashes with RuntimeError. The entire session is lost, wasting all tokens consumed up to that point.

Scope:

* In the Codex app-server integration, detect tool call failures (non-zero exit, error response)
* Retry the failed tool call up to 2 times with the error message fed back to the model
* If all retries fail, mark the turn as failed but continue the session (let the model try a different approach)
* Only crash the session if the model itself is unreachable or returns malformed output

Validation:

- [ ] A failed tool call is retried before crashing the session
- [ ] Tool call error messages are fed back to the model for self-correction
- [ ] Session continues after a tool call failure (does not crash)

title: [CHILD] Preserve workspace state across retry attempts
description:
Finding from ANQ-103/104 log analysis.

Problem: When a session crashes and retries, the workspace is recreated from scratch (fresh git clone + npm ci). Any partial progress from the previous attempt is lost. The WORKFLOW template says "Continue from current workspace state" but the workspace is actually wiped.

Scope:

* In `workspace.ex`, check if an existing workspace exists for the issue before creating a new one
* If a workspace exists with uncommitted changes, preserve it and let the retry continue from that state
* Only create a fresh workspace if no previous workspace exists or if explicitly requested
* Log whether a retry is using an existing or fresh workspace

Validation:

- [ ] Retry attempts reuse existing workspace with uncommitted changes
- [ ] Fresh clone only happens on first attempt or after workspace corruption
- [ ] Workspace state is logged at retry start
